modalities.value: natively multimodal; text and multiple images

source.quote: Llama Guard 4 is a natively multimodal safety classifier with 12 billion parameters trained jointly on text and multiple images.

languages.value: English and multilingual (French, German, Hindi, Italian, Portuguese, Spanish, Thai)

source.quote: French, German, Hindi, Italian, Portuguese, Spanish, and Thai
The model has 12 billion parameters in total and uses an early fusion transformer architecture with dense layers to keep the overall size small.

architecture.value: dense early-fusion transformer pruned from Llama 4 Scout MoE (shared expert retained)

source.quote: The model has 12 billion parameters in total and uses an early fusion transformer architecture with dense layers to keep the overall size small.

trainingData.value: blend of Llama Guard 3-8B and Llama Guard 3-11B-vision data, plus multi-image and multilingual data; roughly 3:1 text-only to multimodal

source.quote: We blend the training data from both modalities, with a ratio of roughly 3:1 text-only data to multimodal data containing one or more images.

topics.headline: Classifies prompts and responses as safe or unsafe against MLCommons hazard taxonomy S1–S14

source.quote: it generates text in its output that indicates whether a given prompt or response is safe or unsafe, and if unsafe, it also lists the content categories violated.

topics.headline: Hazard category S4: Child Sexual Exploitation
May be susceptible to adversarial attacks that could bypass intended use

topics.headline: May be susceptible to prompt injection; points to Prompt Guard 2

source.quote: Llama Guard 4 may be susceptible to adversarial attacks or prompt injection attacks that could bypass or alter its intended use

topics.headline: Additional category S14 Code Interpreter Abuse for text-only tool-call use cases

source.quote: We include an additional category, Code Interpreter Abuse, for text-only tool-call use cases.

topics.headline: Covers cyber crimes under S2 and Code Interpreter Abuse under S14
S9 Indiscriminate Weapons includes chemical and biological weapons

source.quote: including: (1) chemical weapons (ex: nerve gas), (2) biological weapons (ex: anthrax)

findings.text: Llama Guard 4 roughly matches or exceeds Llama Guard 3 overall on input and output filtering for English, multilingual text, and mixed text and images.

source.quote: We find that Llama Guard 4 roughly matches or exceeds the overall performance of the Llama Guard 3 models on both input and output filtering, for English and multilingual text and for mixed text and images.

findings.text: In some internal tests, input filtering cut safety violations and raised refusal rate more than output filtering.

source.quote: In some internal tests we have found that input filtering reduces safety violation rate and raises overall refusal rate more than output filtering does, but your experience may vary.

findings.text: The card omits evals against competitor models because they are typically not aligned with this classifier's safety policy.

source.quote: We omit evals against competitor models, which are typically not aligned with the specific safety policy that this classifier was trained on, limiting our ability to make direct comparisons.

findings.text: For the multi-image baseline, only the final image was fed to Llama Guard 3-11B-vision, which does not support multiple images.

source.quote: For multi-image prompts, only the final image was input into Llama Guard 3-11B-vision, which does not support multiple images.

findings.text: S5 Defamation, S8 Intellectual Property, and S13 Elections may need factual, up-to-date knowledge beyond what this classifier provides alone.

source.quote: Some hazard categories may require factual, up-to-date knowledge to be evaluated fully (for example, [S5] Defamation, [S8] Intellectual Property, and [S13] Elections).

findings.text: Performance was tested mostly with prompts of a few images (three most often); results may differ with many more images.

source.quote: the performance of Llama Guard 4 was tested mostly with prompts containing a few images (three, most frequently), so performance may vary if using it to classify safety with a much larger number of images.

findings.text: As a large language model (LLM) classifier, it may be bypassed by adversarial or prompt-injection attacks; Meta points users to Prompt Guard 2.

source.quote: Llama Guard 4 may be susceptible to adversarial attacks or prompt injection attacks that could bypass or alter its intended use: see Prompt Guard 2
